newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine court halts water privatisation process.
newsitem.headline: Philippine court halts water privatisation process.

text.p: The Philippine Court of Appeals said on Friday it had issued orders temporarily halting the privatisation of the Manila waterworks system, including final endorsement by President Fidel Ramos of the winning bids.
The country's Metropolitan Water and Sewerage System (MWSS) awarded two 25-year contracts to operate the Manila utility to two large consortia last week.
The contracts are said to involve investment of at least $7 billion, one of the largest waterworks privatisations in the world.

A three-judge appeals panel, responding to a group petition which said Ramos's authority to privatise the utility had lapsed, said the MWSS was halted from any act furthering the privatisation until further orders.
It also ordered the MWSS to respond to the petition within 10 days.
The group had earlier approached the Manila Regional Trial Court to halt the announcement of the winning bids, but the judge refused to issue a preliminary injunction.

The group, which includes the governor of Rizal province near Manila, a retired politician, businessmen and other concerned citizens, has said Ramos's authority to privatise the MWSS under the Water Crisis Act lapsed in December 1995.
Angel Lazaro, the MWSS adminstrator, said the petitioners' case was flawed.
"Obviously, we do not agree that the Water Crisis Act has lapsed, otherwise we wouldn't have pushed through with the bidding," he told Reuters.
One of the two contracts was won by a consortium including Philippine conglomerate Ayala Corp and its partners Bechtel Corp of the United States and British firm United Utilities.
The other winning bid was posted by a combine including local firm Benpres Holdings Corp and its French partner Lyonnaise des Eaux SA.
Officials from Ayala and Benpres said they had no immediate comment on the court ruling.

The court said the injunction was aimed at preventing the petition being rendered "moot and academic" and it specifically prohibited the government's Committee on Privatisation from passing on the contracts to Ramos for final approval until further orders.
Earlier on Friday, the commission said it had endorsed the winning bids and committee chairman and Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said the papers were being forwarded to Ramos.
It is the latest in a series of high-profile projects in the Philippines to be mired in litigation or other problems.

Among the projects under a cloud are the privatisation of a container terminal at Subic Bay, the sale of the historic Manila Hotel, a project to develop reclaimed land in Manila Bay and and the construction of what will perhaps ultimately be the country's biggest power plant.
